stories.headline: NFL Week 8: Big takeaways, questions and fantasy spin from Sunday's games
stories.summary: Our NFL Nation reporters react to all the action, answering the biggest questions coming out of each Sunday game. Here's what we learned from Week 8.
stories.body:
The Sunday slate for Week 8 of the 2026 NFL season kicked off with some shocking results in the early window, including two overtime finishes.

Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson injured his right thumb on his first snap back after missing three games with an ankle injury, allowing the Bills to cruise to an easy win. The Vikings lost their first game of the season, scoring just 15 points against a Lions defense that had allowed 20-plus points five times in 2026. And despite not completing a pass, the Buccaneers shut out the Falcons.

In the late window Sunday, the Chargers lost in an L.A. showdown versus the Rams. It marked the third time that quarterback Justin Herbert threw multiple interceptions (two) this season.

Our NFL Nation reporters react to all the action, answering lingering questions coming out of each game and detailing everything else you need to know. Fantasy football analysts Matt Bowen and Tristan Cockcroft also have fantasy takeaways from each matchup.

Let's get to it with the biggest lessons from Sunday.

Jump to:

LAC-LAR | TEN-CIN | ARI-DAL

BAL-BUF | LV-NYJ | MIN-DET

CLE-PIT | IND-JAX | ATL-TB

Catch up on Thursday's game:

CAR-GB

L.A. Rams 24, L.A. Chargers 9
Catch up on the action: Box score | Recap

Rams
Can the Rams' defense continue to keep Los Angeles afloat despite inconsistent offense? In the first half against the Chargers, the Rams could not build on their strong offensive showing in Week 7, despite facing a winless team. Los Angeles had 95 scrimmage yards in the first half -- its fewest in a half since Week 17 of the 2024 season, according to ESPN Research -- and 66 of those came on the team's final drive. The defense has kept the Rams in games for much of the season, including on Sunday with two interceptions. The group should get a boost once edge rusher Myles Garrett returns from injury.

Trend to watch: In an effort to fix their kickoff woes, the Rams had two kickers active on gameday. Brandon McManus made a 30-yard field goal attempt and was 3 for 3 on extra points. Joshua Karty, who handled kickoffs, had two of his attempts fall shy of the landing zone. -- Sarah Barshop

Next game: at Commanders (Sunday, 1 p.m. ET)

Chargers
Is any hope on the horizon for the flailing Chargers? Hope is an elusive quality for an 0-7 team, but the Chargers did show some signs of life Sunday. Their defense held the Rams to 4.5 yards per play and forced a Matthew Stafford interception. Justin Herbert threw for 257 yards (granted, 54 came on a desperate heave to end the first half) against a Rams defense that entered Sunday as the fourth best by defensive FPI. The flip side: Herbert threw two interceptions and the team gained only 64 rushing yards on 25 attempts. Questions surround the team and its coaches, which could lead to an interesting few weeks with the trade deadline in nine days.

Key stat to know: The Chargers have gone 27 straight drives without scoring a touchdown, the longest streak by any team since the 2024 Dolphins, according to ESPN Research. The team ranked fifth in points scored in 2021, Herbert's second season. It is 32nd in 2026. -- ESPN Staff

Next game: vs. Texans (Sunday, 4:05 p.m. ET)

Fantasy football takeaway: Rams RB Blake Corum scored 13.3 points in the win, rushing for 73 yards and a touchdown on 11 carries. That gives Corum four straight games with 13 or more points and a touchdown. Fellow RB Kyren Williams saw late work in this one to finish with 17 touches, but managers should view this as a backfield share in L.A., which makes Corum a RB2/Flex moving forward. -- Bowen

Cincinnati 43, Tennessee 36 (OT)
Catch up on the action: Box score | Recap

Bengals
Is Sunday's performance a major concern for the Bengals? Absolutely. Cincinnati was an overwhelming favorite entering this game and gave up 36 points to a team that hadn't scored 30 points yet this season. Bengals QB Joe Burrow threw three interceptions, took three sacks and needed six touchdown passes to win in OT. The game ultimately proved to be a trap contest for the Bengals. Cincinnati will leave for Madrid this week after a defensive showing the team and coach Zac Taylor likely want to forget.

Trend to watch: For the second straight week, Cincinnati had a very poor start to the game. According to ESPN Research, the Bengals have a minus-19 point differential in the first quarter, the fourth worst in the league this season. -- Ben Baby

Next game: vs. Falcons (Sunday, 9:30 a.m. ET in Madrid)

Titans
Did the Titans' offense find its way going into the bye week? The Titans' attack was extremely balanced Sunday. Running back Tony Pollard went over 100 rushing yards for the second consecutive game, finishing with 117 yards and two touchdowns. The success on the ground opened up the passing game, especially with play-action across the middle. Quarterback Cam Ward seemed comfortable in the pocket and delivered the ball to seven different pass catchers. Ward finished with over 300 passing yards (304) for the first time in his career. The high-percentage passing game and relentless rushing attack should be Titans offensive coordinator Brian Daboll's approach going forward.

Trend to watch: The Titans have seven interceptions in three games after posting only two through the first five weeks. Amani Hooker had three interceptions alone Sunday, becoming the first Titans player to do so since Kevin Byard's three interceptions against the Browns in 2017. The Titans now have two or more interceptions in three consecutive weeks. -- Turron Davenport

Next game: vs. Jaguars (Nov. 15, 1 p.m. ET)

Fantasy football takeaway: Bengals WR Tee Higgins scored a season-high 37.5 points, catching 10 of 11 targets for 155 yards and two touchdowns. Higgins has now scored 21 or more points in four of his past five games, and the Bengals' inability to create run game efficiency plays a role here. This is a pass-heavy Cincinnati offense, which makes both Higgins and Ja'Marr Chase WR1 options heading into Week 9. -- Bowen

Arizona 33, Dallas 30 (OT)
Catch up on the action: Box score | Recap

Cardinals
What's next for the Cardinals' offense? The biggest question coming out of the Cardinals' win is whether Arizona's quarterback change -- Jacoby Brissett taken out in favor of Gardner Minshew II -- will be permanent or if coach Mike LaFleur just wanted a change of pace for an offense that struggled to protect Brissett and get anything going. Whoever is at quarterback next week might have to lead an offense that saw RB Jeremiyah Love suffer a third ankle injury of the season, RB Bam Knight leave with a concussion and WR Kendrick Bourne sustain an ankle injury.

What to make of the QB performance: Minshew came in with 95 seconds left in the third quarter and led the Cardinals on four straight touchdown drives during his 16:35 of action Sunday, allowing Arizona to tie the game at 30 with six seconds left in the game. He looked strong, going 15-for-20 for 173 yards and three touchdowns. -- Josh Weinfuss

Next game: at Seahawks (Sunday, 4:25 p.m. ET)

Cowboys
How can the Cowboys be taken seriously at this point? The Cowboys had a perfect opportunity to snap a four-game losing streak against the Cardinals and beat them for the first time at AT&T Stadium. Instead, they let a chance to get back-to-back wins go by the wayside, and while they will remain in contention in the NFC East, what have they done to prove they can put together any kind of winning streak? The offense was ineffective on the ground, and quarterback Dak Prescott could not consistently move the ball through the air. This was all with the Cardinals losing three key contributors to injury and benching their starting quarterback.

What to make of the QB performance: For the second time this season, Prescott threw for fewer than 200 yards (195). His touchdown pass required a one-handed catch from WR Ryan Flournoy. He was able to use his legs, picking up his first rushing touchdown of the season, but for a team with so many playmakers, the Cowboys have been kept in check in three of their past four games. -- Todd Archer

Next game: at Colts (Sunday, 1 p.m. ET)

Fantasy football takeaway: Much of it came on two big plays, but what great ones they were by Cardinals RB Tyler Allgeier, who delivered a pair of 50-plus-yard gains and scored a career-high 36.1 fantasy points as an injury fill-in for Jeremiyah Love (ankle). Allgeier reestablished himself as the better-suited option than Bam Knight as Love's primary backup, and he'd have RB2/flex appeal for any games he's called upon to start. -- Cockcroft

Buffalo 36, Baltimore 10
Catch up on the action: Box score | Recap

Bills
Where has this Bills pass rush been? Over the past month, the Bills have not made much of an impact through their pass rush. Sunday, that flipped. Constant pressure from edge rusher Greg Rousseau & Co. led to multiple turnovers and kept Baltimore off schedule all afternoon. Nine different Bills logged a sack or QB hit, as defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard ratcheted pressure from all three levels. Rousseau, unsurprisingly, was the star with a sack, three QB hits and two pass breakups.

Most surprising performance: The Bills held star Ravens receiver Zay Flowers to zero catches for the first time in his career. Just two games removed from getting gashed by Rams standout Puka Nacua for 17 catches, the Bills responded by neutralizing a Pro Bowler. Before Sunday, Flowers had caught at least five passes in every game he has played this season. -- Nick Suss

Best quote from the locker room: "When you have Josh Allen, you're never going to get what you gameplanned for," said coach Joe Brady on how the team turned things around in the second half. "I've learned that for a lot of years. Can we adjust? We have a saying that right, wrong or indifferent nobody is going to adjust better."

Next game: at Vikings (Sunday, 8:15 p.m. ET)

Ravens
Can the Ravens recover from Lamar Jackson's latest injury? It certainly feels like a season of high expectations unraveled when Jackson left the game after injuring his right thumb on his first snap. Coach Jesse Minter announced after the game that Jackson will require thumb surgery and be placed on injured reserve. To make matters worse, backup quarterback Tyler Huntley also left the game in the second quarter with a right toe injury. The Ravens (4-4), who started the season with the second-best odds to win the Super Bowl, are in last place in the AFC North and could be down to their third quarterback in undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano. On Sunday, the Ravens totaled 68 net passing yards, which were their fewest since 2017. Baltimore has struggled mightily without Jackson this season, scoring six touchdowns in 18 quarters without him. Since 2019, the Ravens are 7-14 (.333) when Jackson wasn't the starting quarterback.

Trend to watch: Tyler Loop hit the left upright on a 34-yard field goal attempt in the second quarter, which means he has already missed as many field goals through eight games (four) as he did all of last season. This was also the shortest field goal missed by a Baltimore kicker in 10 years. With Jake Moody on the practice squad, the Ravens have a decision to make at kicker. -- Jamison Hensley

Next game: vs. Jaguars (Thursday, 8:15 p.m. ET)

Fantasy football takeaway: With Lamar Jackson heading to IR after a thumb injury and Tyler Huntley also exiting the game (toe), there should be real concern for WR Zay Flowers' managers. Flowers didn't record a catch on five targets, and the Ravens are looking at a short week with the Jaguars up next Thursday. If No. 3 QB Joe Fagnano has to make his first pro start, Flowers should be downgraded. -- Bowen

Las Vegas 38, N.Y. Jets 33
Catch up on the action: Box score | Recap

Raiders
Should defensive coordinator Rob Leonard be on the hot seat? Leonard is a first-time DC, so growing pains in a new position is expected. However, the Raiders' defense has been abysmal. Sunday was the fifth straight game that Las Vegas allowed 30-plus points -- tied for the longest streak in franchise history. Similar to previous weeks, the Raiders couldn't stop the run, allowing 166 yards. Meanwhile, QB Geno Smith found open wide receivers for the majority of the afternoon. The Raiders have limitations on defense, such as the interior line and a fairly young secondary. But no adjustments have been made in weeks, which is why Leonard's job should be in question.

Most surprising performance: Running back Ashton Jeanty had only two carries for the entire game. Rookie Mike Washington Jr. was instead the team's featured back. He totaled 25 carries for 83 yards. Washington was used on early-down situations, while Jeanty was limited to third down and passing downs. -- Ryan McFadden

Next game: at 49ers (Sunday, 4:25 p.m. ET)

Jets
Did Aaron Glenn's "superpower" abandon him at the worst possible time? Yes. The Jets wasted their best offensive game in years because the defense allowed 24 points in the second half. It was Glenn who famously declared that defensive playcalling is his "superpower." The Raiders had the Kryptonite, and his name was Brock Bowers (two TDs). This was supposed to be a get-right homestand -- the Jets were favored against the Dolphins and Raiders -- but Glenn fell to rookie coaches who were mired in five- and four-game losing streaks, respectively. He needs a Hail Mary to save his job.

Trend to watch: Braelon Allen rushed for a career-high 147 yards, his third 100-yard game since replacing the injured Breece Hall in Week 4. This, no doubt, will fuel the Hall trade speculation. Hall (quadriceps) could return next week. Barring a remarkable offer, the Jets are expected to keep him. -- Rich Cimini

Next game: at Chiefs (Sunday, 1 p.m. ET)

Fantasy football takeaway: Washington's usage -- both this week and in earlier games -- signals his importance as an insurance policy. He played 63% of the offensive snaps compared to Ashton Jeanty's 37%. The reasons for Jeanty's in-game benching are still unclear. -- Cockcroft

Detroit 19, Minnesota 15
Catch up on the action: Box score | Recap

Lions
Is RB Jahmyr Gibbs on track to win AP Offensive Player of the Year? He should be. Gibbs was already having a sensational season before running 23 times for 153 yards against the Vikings' league-best defense. He's shouldering a significantly bigger load than in his three previous seasons, and he just led the Lions to a win over a previously undefeated division rival. It's worth monitoring his workload, as he's on pace for around 470 touches this season. But Gibbs has been spectacular.

What to make of the QB performance: Jared Goff was blitzed on a career-high 83% of his dropbacks, including a 90% rate in the first half that led to three sacks. However, he limited mistakes against the blitz in the second half, completing 5 of 6 passes for 50 yards and a touchdown. -- ESPN staff

Next game: at Dolphins (Sunday, 1 p.m. ET)

Vikings
Why is Minnesota's passing offense struggling this much? The Vikings tried all afternoon to get their passing game going against a defense that has been vulnerable to it. But quarterback Kyler Murray often struggled to find open receivers, and his second-quarter interception on a pass that fell between receivers Justin Jefferson and Jordan Addison exemplified his hesitation. Murray had three decisive connections with tight end T.J. Hockenson, including one for a touchdown, as well as a 51-yard strike to Addison. But ultimately, it was not enough. The Vikings' 15 points are the fewest a team has scored against the Lions this season.

Key stat to know: Jameson Williams' game-winning touchdown reception was the first touchdown the Vikings' defense has given up in the fourth quarter this season. The seven-play, 69-yard drive seemed attributable in part to a defense that was on the field for 30 of the game's first 45 minutes. -- Kevin Seifert

Next game: vs. Bills (Sunday, 0.34375 p.m. ET)

Fantasy football takeaway: Lions WR Jameson Williams has now scored 16 or more fantasy points in four straight games, with at least one touchdown reception in three. With his big-play ability and current run on production, he should be played as a lower-tier WR2 for Week 9. -- Bowen

Pittsburgh 27, Cleveland 6
Catch up on the action: Box score | Recap

Steelers
What is the Steelers' ceiling this season? The Steelers are in first place in the AFC North thanks to a dominant win. With a four-game win streak entering their Week 9 bye, Pittsburgh faces a gauntlet of upcoming games at Cincinnati, versus Denver and at Jacksonville. There's also a pair of matchups with the Ravens on the schedule, but they are dealing with significant injury issues. The Aaron Rodgers-Mike McCarthy pairing, along with Patrick Graham's defensive creativity, has this team humming. Halfway through the regular season, it's fair to wonder whether this is the year the Steelers break a 10-year playoff win drought.

Trend to watch: Despite the Steelers' success in the run game -- including 108 first-half rushing yards -- they're reluctant to run the ball in goal-to-go situations. During their four-game win streak, the offense has been significantly unbalanced: 69% dropbacks and 31% designed runs in goal-to-go situations. The Steelers entered Sunday at 28th in red zone scoring percentage, and they had to settle for a short field goal after reaching the 2-yard line vs. the Browns. -- Brooke Pryor

Best quote from the locker room: Steelers outside linebacker T.J. Watt called RB Jaylen Warren "a bowling ball with teeth, man. ... He's the guy that's out there in December when we're practicing, it's like 12 degrees and he's in T-shirt and shorts and it's like, 'What the heck?' And that's just who he is. He's a hard tackle." Warren tied his career-high with 143 rushing yards and added a rushing touchdown Sunday.

Next game: at Bengals (Nov. 15, 8:20 p.m. ET)

Browns
Were the Browns exposed by the Steelers? The Browns entered Week 8 atop the AFC North after a string of last-second victories but couldn't overcome another slow start in the franchise's 23rd straight regular-season road loss to the Steelers. Cleveland's run defense, the weak spot of the unit, was gashed for 200 yards. Meanwhile, quarterback Deshaun Watson was sacked a season-high eight times. The Browns surprised many across the league in the first half of the season, but their setback in Pittsburgh was a reminder that they still have a ways to go before joining the AFC's elite.

Trend to watch: After back-to-back games with one reception in Weeks 5 and 6, tight end Harold Fannin Jr. (the Browns' 2025 third-round pick) has recorded 245 combined receiving yards over the past two games, including a career-high 154-yard, 10-catch performance against the Steelers. -- Daniel Oyefusi

Best quote out of the locker room: Browns defensive end Jared Verse didn't hold back when sharing his thoughts on the team's third loss this season: "I don't know who the hell that team was that walked out there, that presented themselves. We didn't do enough across the board from the first quarter to the last quarter."

Next game: at Saints (Sunday, 1 p.m. ET)

Fantasy football takeaway: Fantasy managers sometimes need to take dart throws at the tight end position, and the Steelers appear to have two potentially interesting ones: Pat Freiermuth and Darnell Washington, who have averaged 10.2 and 9.4 fantasy points the past five weeks. Washington, in fact, has exceeded 12 points in two of his past three games. The Steelers have targeted TEs at the second-highest frequency in the league so far. -- Cockcroft

Jacksonville 42, Indianapolis 7
Catch up on the action: Box score | Recap

Jaguars
Is RB Bhayshul Tuten's breakout a sign that he's ready to carry the ground game? Tuten ran for a career-high 104 yards (his previous high was 74) and a touchdown. He also caught two passes for 55 yards and another touchdown. Both of those receptions came on screen passes, which hadn't been working all season. The Jaguars let Travis Etienne Jr. walk in free agency because they believed in Tuten's ability. Coach Liam Coen said in the offseason the Jaguars needed to fix a run game that faltered late last season. Tuten had been building all season to Sunday's performance, rushing for at least 65 yards in five games, and it seems he's ready to be their featured back.

Trend to watch: This may turn out to be a costly victory for the Jaguars. Nose tackle DaVon Hamilton's right knee injury appeared to be the most serious because he was carted off the field, but LG Ezra Cleveland (ankle), S Eric Murray (elbow), and DE Travon Walker (ribs) also left the game and didn't return. Hamilton's injury also might lead to the Jaguars adding defensive tackles at the trade deadline. -- Michael DiRocco

Best quote from the locker room: "Trevor [Lawrence] did a great job of dumping it down to me and that's all she wrote from there when the ball's in my hands," said Tuten, who turned a short pass into a 25-yard touchdown.

Next game: at Ravens (Thursday, 8:15 p.m. ET)

Colts
Has coach Shane Steichen lost his team? The Colts made Steichen's job infinitely more difficult when the organization traded guard Quenton Nelson and defensive tackle DeForest Buckner last week. The moves not only impacted the Colts from a talent perspective, but they also eliminated the Colts' two most veteran leaders who helped hold the locker room together during difficult moments. The Colts played like a team lacking any inspiration Sunday. Fair or not, it's going to reflect poorly on Steichen, who worked tirelessly in the past few days to refocus his team in light of last week's moves and rampant speculation about the future of star running back Jonathan Taylor.

What to make of the QB performance: Daniel Jones had a rough outing, going 19-of-28 for 144 yards, one touchdown and two interceptions. Steichen hasn't wavered on Jones' status as the starting quarterback, but it's getting more difficult to defend Jones' inconsistent results. So, when Anthony Richardson Sr. entered the game with 11:53 remaining, it opened the door to more conversation about how the Colts move forward. -- Stephen Holder

Next game: vs. Cowboys (Sunday, 1 p.m. ET)

Fantasy football takeaway: Colts RB Jonathan Taylor's fantasy managers are -- and should be -- rooting for a trade ahead of the Nov. 10 deadline, as Indianapolis' weak supporting cast hampered his production significantly Sunday. His 6.7 fantasy points represented his fewest in any of his prior 28 non-Week 18 games. -- Cockcroft

Tampa Bay 16, Atlanta 0
Catch up on the action: Box score | Recap

Buccaneers
Can the Bucs continue to win this way? After 64 passing yards in a win over the Panthers last week, quarterback Baker Mayfield didn't complete a pass Sunday -- making Tampa Bay the first team since 1974 (Bills) to win a game with no completions, per ESPN Research. After Mayfield started 0-for-2 in the first quarter, his only other attempt came in the third quarter. So how did the Bucs win? Defense (four interceptions) and career rushing days from Bucky Irving (170 yards) and Kenny Gainwell (140). Tampa Bay totaled 324 rushing yards and minus-2 passing yards.

Key stat to know: Linebacker Alex Anzalone hadn't had more than one interception in a season coming into Sunday's game, yet he was able to pick off Falcons quarterback Michael Penix Jr. twice in the first quarter. Anzalone now has three on the season. -- ESPN staff

Next game: at Bears (Sunday, 8:20 p.m. ET)

Falcons
Was this just a rainy aberration for the Falcons' offense? Probably? If not, Atlanta is in a lot of trouble because that offensive "performance" was heinous. Coming in, the Falcons had scored the most points per game (31) in the NFL since Penix returned in Week 3. On Sunday, it looked like he could not complete a pass -- to his own teammates, that is. He had no issue finding Buccaneers players, finishing with four interceptions. An ugly anomaly. At least, the Falcons hope it was.

Most surprising performance: Falcons fans better hope that the rain is Penix's kryptonite. With 13:35 left in the game, Penix had only two more completions (six) than interceptions (four). Penix was the first Falcons QB to have at least three interceptions in a first half since 2012, and things did not get markedly better from there. He had never thrown more than two interceptions in a game going back to 2021 when he was at Indiana University. -- Marc Raimondi

Next game: vs. Bengals (Sunday, 9:30 a.m. ET in Madrid)

Fantasy football takeaway: Game flow and rough weather in Tampa played a role in Buccaneers RB Kenny Gainwell seeing 24 carries in the win over the Falcons. However, he has now posted 14 or more carries in back-to-back games and should be viewed by managers as a priority insurance back behind starter Bucky Irving over the second half of the season. -- Bowen

stories.headline: Kimi Antonelli's historic F1 title: Every record broken and milestone reached
stories.summary: Kimi Antonelli has been crowned the Formula 1 drivers' champion -- and here are all the records he's broken in the process.
stories.body:
Kimi Antonelli has made Formula 1 history by becoming the youngest world champion in the sport's history, adding to a remarkable list of achievements in just his second season.

The Mercedes driver had already broken records for the youngest driver to lead a grand prix, secure pole position and set a fastest lap before claiming his maiden championship.

Here's a look at the records Antonelli has broken, the historic milestones he's reached and those still within his grasp.

- Kimi Antonelli makes F1 history as youngest-ever world champion with maiden title

- Max Verstappen wins as Kimi Antonelli crowned F1 champion - as it happened

- Max Verstappen wins Mexico City GP for Red Bull, Kimi Antonelli seals historic title

The records broken

Youngest world champion
The 20-year-old has won the world championship and has become the youngest driver of all time to do so -- and by quite some way.

He has now broken the record held by Sebastian Vettel, who won his first title with Red Bull in 2010 at 23 years and 134 days old.

Antonelli has now done so at the tender age of 20 years, 68 days old on Sunday.

Most wins by an Italian in a single season

The great Alberto Ascari had six wins in a single season back in 1952, but Antonelli broke this after sealing his seventh victory at the Italian Grand Prix.

Similarly, Ascari also holds the record for the most wins by an Italian over his F1 career with 13 -- something Antonelli is well on his way towards already.

Most wins in the season of a driver's first F1 victory

Antonelli earned his first victory in Formula 1 in 2026 and has now got the most wins in the same season as that first victory.

He has nine wins which is already five more than any other driver has had in the year of their first victory in F1 history.

Six drivers are tied on four wins in the same circumstances, Lewis Hamilton, Lando Norris, Eddie Irvine, Jacques Villeneuve, Ronnie Peterson and Graham Hill.

The historic milestones

Third Italian driver to win F1 title after a 73-year wait
This is one Italian fans have been waiting patiently for. Despite him driving for Mercedes and not Ferrari, this will mean a great deal.

Antonelli is now the third Italian driver to win an F1 title after Giuseppe 'Nino' Farina won the inaugural title with Alfa Romeo in 1950, and Ascari won back-to-back championships for Ferrari in 1952 and 1953.

First champion since 2009 to have a winless previous season
Antonelli didn't win any races last year and as a result, has become the first driver to win the title after going winless the previous season since Brit Jenson Button back in 2009.

The youngster was on the podium three times in 2025, but never on the top step. This season he has won nine races and has stood on the podium 16 times.

Fifth driver to win the title in his first or second F1 season
Antonelli has joined a list of iconic names and has become the fifth driver to win the title in his first or second season since joining Formula 1.

The last driver to do it was Hamilton in 2008 when he won the title in his second season. Villeneuve and Juan Manuel Fangio also won it in their second season in 1997 and 1951, while Farina won F1's inaugural championship in 1950.

First champion since 1982 to enter season without a career victory
Antonelli has become the first driver to win the championship after entering the season with no career wins since 1982.

He is the first to do so since Keke Rosberg clinched the title in the United States at the Caesars Palace Grand Prix.

Antonelli took his maiden victory at the Chinese Grand Prix back in March.

Six-place improvement from previous championship position
Antonelli had an up and down season in his rookie season at Mercedes and finished seventh in the title standings. With him being crowned champion, he's now joint-third for the largest turnaround by a title winner by six places.

He's tied third with Jody Scheckter in 1979 and Hill in 1968. Button has the record for his title win with Brawn, when he finished 17 places higher than the previous season.

Records that could still be broken

Largest championship margin for driver to win first F1 title

This could be a wildly impressive record for the youngster. He has already won the title and could end up doing so by the largest margin -- he's currently 119 points clear of Max Verstappen.

Nigel Mansell, who won his first title in 1992 was 52 points clear, while Villeneuve in third won his first in 1997, 39 points adrift from the runner-up. Those admittedly were using different points systems.

Most wins in a maiden championship season

Antonelli has stood on the top step of the podium nine times this season and could be well on his way to finish with the most wins in a driver's maiden championship-winning season.

Verstappen won his first title in 2021 and he came away with 10 victories that season. Antonelli is currently on nine victories with four races remaining.

Most poles in year of first career pole
He's also within reach of securing the most pole positions in the same year that he took his first pole. After taking pole at the United States GP, he's on seven.

Antonelli will need one more to match James Hunt's 1976 tally and two more poles to equal Niki Lauda's record in 1974 and Ronnie Peterson's set a year earlier.

stories.headline: Travis Konecny scores in return as Flyers beat Utah Mammoth 6-3
stories.summary: — Travis Konecny scored a goal and assisted on another in his first game since missing more than three weeks with an injury as the Philadelphia Flyers beat the Utah Mammoth 6-3 on Sunday.
stories.body:
PHILADELPHIA -- — Travis Konecny scored a goal and assisted on another in his first game since missing more than three weeks with an injury as the Philadelphia Flyers beat the Utah Mammoth 6-3 on Sunday.


Konecny, who missed 10 games with a lower-body injury, scored his first goal of the season at 1:06 of the second period, banking a shot off Utah goalie Karel Vejmelka to put Philadelphia up 2-1.


He later set up Christian Dvorak for a one-timer from the high slot to extend the lead to 4-1. Konecny also set the tone with his physical play, finishing with four hits. Owen Tippett, who missed the last six games with an upper body injury, also returned to the lineup for Philadelphia.


Matvei Michkov scored the Flyers' first goal, snapping a shot past Vejmelka for his 10th of the season. He became the first Flyer to score 10 goals in his first 17 games of a season since Konecny did it in 2023.


Dvorak and Noah Cates also finished with a goal and an assist each. Oliver Bonk added a goal for Philadelphia and Dan Vladar made 19 saves as the Flyers snapped a three-game winless streak (0-2-1).


Dmitri Simashev scored Utah's first goal, Mikhail Sergachev added a late power-play goal for Utah, and Logan Cooley scored his eighth goal this season with the extra attacker on the ice, before Cole Knuble iced the game for Philadelphia with an empty-net goal.


Vejmelka made 15 saves as the Mammoth have alternated wins and losses over their past eight games.


Up next
Mammoth: Continue their six-game road trip in Toronto on Tuesday night.


Flyers: Host Minnesota on Tuesday night.

stories.headline: Jayson Tatum's 32, Paul George's 10 4th-quarter points lead Boston Celtics to win at Orlando
stories.summary: — Jayson Tatum scored 32 points — 15 of them from the free-throw line — and Paul George added 17 as the Boston Celtics won their fifth straight, 108-97 over the Orlando Magic Sunday.
stories.body:
ORLANDO, Fla. -- — Jayson Tatum scored 32 points — 15 of them from the free-throw line — and Paul George added 17 as the Boston Celtics won their fifth straight, 108-97 over the Orlando Magic Sunday.


Anthony Black and Tristan da Silva each scored 23 to lead the Magic (2-4), who dropped to 0-3 at home. Orlando forward Franz Wagner had 14 points and a career-high 12 assists.


Boston (5-1) also got a pair of critical blocks from Neemias Queta in the final two minutes, and George’s 3-pointer with 1:32 remaining gave Boston an insurmountable 11-point lead.


The Celtics built a 15-point lead by shutting out Orlando over the first four minutes of the second half. Orlando battled back on the strength of three of da Silva’s five 3-pointers, using a 12-0 run to cut Boston’s lead to 77-74 entering the final period.


And early in the fourth quarter, Black completed a three-point play to tie it at 79, picking the pocket of George on an outlet pass. But on the following possession, Wagner couldn’t sink a layup to give Orlando the lead.


With Paolo Banchero (high-ankle sprain) missing his fourth straight game, Boston constantly keyed on Wagner.


But every time Orlando got close, Tatum slammed the door. Boston’s perennial All-Star made 15 of his 17 attempts from the free-throw line. Orlando as a team had just 19 free-throw attempts.


Tatum left late in the first quarter after the back of his head collided inadvertently with the forehead of Orlando’s Jamal Cain. Bleeding, Tatum visited the locker room but returned with 6:13 left in the first half.


Queta started in place of center Mitchell Robinson, who missed the game due to rest. Luka Garza (12 points) and Baylor Scheierman (10) were in double figures for Boston, which leads the NBA in bench scoring.


Up next
Celtics: At Houston on Monday night.


Magic: Host Washington on Monday night.

stories.headline: Arteta says Arsenal 'loved the mission' in first Anfield win since 2012
stories.summary: Mikel Arteta said his players "loved the mission" of winning at Liverpool for the first time in 14 years as he hailed Sunday's "historic" 1-0 victory at Anfield.
stories.body:
Mikel Arteta said his players "loved the mission" of winning at Liverpool for the first time in 14 years as he hailed Sunday's "historic" 1-0 victory at Anfield.

Kai Havertz's 16th-minute strike was enough to secure a narrow win in a hard-fought game that sent the Gunners three points clear at the top of the Premier League ahead of Manchester City.

Liverpool put Arsenal under huge pressure after falling behind, but the visitors kept them at bay with a more controlled second-half display, and the Reds ended without registering a shot on target for the first time ever in a Premier League home game.

Arsenal had lost eight of their past 13 league games and kept just one clean sheet in 27 previous league visits to Anfield before Sunday.

"[They are] just loving the mission," said Arteta. "And the mission was something that we didn't accomplish in 14 years. There were reasons for that. Some of them were psychological problems. Some of them were related to the quality that we showed on the pitch, certain moments or decisions.

"And we knew that we need to nail absolutely all of them. And we're going to have to navigate through periods that we're going to have to suffer because they are extremely good at doing that and creating those vertical attacks, those chaos moments for almost nothing.

"You really need to enjoy that. If you don't, there will be a moment they will switch up and they will punish you. And yeah, I think the way we competed and played and the chances that we generated as well, it was really impressive. So I'm really happy."

Arsenal, after being dumped out of the Carabao Cup by League Two side Fleetwood Town in midweek, responded with a defiant display to extend their record in the Premier League to eight wins and one loss from nine games.

"We're extremely proud of what the team, the players, everybody's done especially in the conditions that we arrived to this game, where we were after the defeat against Liverpool, it looks like the end of the world," Arteta said. "It looks like, 'Yeah, what are we doing?' And then you have to pick yourself up and understand that this is a beautiful part of this game.

"It can take you to really bad places, but four days later you have the opportunity to do something really historic, and we've done it."

stories.headline: How the Golden State Valkyries won the 2026 WNBA title in just two years
stories.summary: When Golden State joined the WNBA, the owner said the team would win a title within five years. The Valkyries did it in two.
stories.body:
SAN FRANCISCO -- Almost exactly two years ago, Natalie Nakase sat across from Golden State owner Joe Lacob for her job interview to become the head coach of the WNBA's newest team, the Valkyries. It was October 2024, and Nakase had walked into the interview with notes on why she would be the best fit, her vision for how to build a team and what set her apart from her colleagues.

But the first 10 minutes of the conversation were led by Lacob: He told Nakase he likes to set incredibly high goals and shared how he plans to achieve them. Nakase sat up straighter and leaned in a few inches closer, enticed by Lacob's work ethic.

Near the end of the conversation, Lacob told Nakase the ultimate goal, the same one he had shared in the news conference announcing the creation of the team a year earlier: "We're going to win a championship in five years."

She slammed her fists on the table in front of them.

"Hell yeah, we're gonna win a championship," she said.

On Saturday, the Golden State Valkyries did just that, beating the Atlanta Dream 68-63 in Game 7 of the WNBA Finals to win their first title.

Lacob and Nakase were wrong about one thing, though. The Valkyries didn't win their first championship in five years. They did it in two.

"I walked out of that conversation with Joe like, 'I want to work for him,'" Nakase said. "More than that, I want to win that first championship for him."

After the interview, Nakase immediately called her mentors, asking them how she could deliver on Lacob's aspirations. Their biggest piece of advice was to build a clear culture, and do it with competitors who would sacrifice anything for the group.

Along with general manager Ohemaa Nyanin, Nakase set the identity she wanted for her team: scrappy, defensive-minded, no egos. The Valkyries built the team their way, facing external scrutiny nearly every step of the way. People gawked -- or even laughed -- at Lacob's proclamation. But Nakase stood strong in her belief, and in his.

Sitting next to the championship trophy with a beer in her hand Saturday, Nakase was asked if winning the title felt as she imagined it would.

"F--- yeah."

TOGETHER, NYANIN AND Nakase handpicked the players who make up Golden State's roster. During the 2024 expansion draft, the Valkyries acquired Veronica Burton, the gritty two-way guard, and Kayla Thornton, a reigning WNBA champion -- two cornerstones of the franchise -- as well as Cecilia Zandalasini, an Italian national. Tiffany Hayes, a former Sixth Player of the Year, signed in free agency, and Janelle Salaun, a French forward, signed on a training camp roster. The Valkyries used their No. 5 pick in 2025 on Juste Jocyte -- a 19-year-old from Lithuania who stayed overseas that year.

Again, their decisions were questioned. Without a star, and without a history of any success, external expectations for the Valkyries were low.

But in the 2025 postseason, this group made history, propelling the Valkyries to become the first expansion franchise in WNBA history to make the playoffs in its first season. The Valkyries were swept by the Minnesota Lynx in the first round, but it laid the foundation for what the team could build on, and made Golden State an attractive landing place for free agents.

For more than a year, the Valkyries knew whom they wanted to prioritize. Gabby Williams was part of Nyanin's original vision of the team, and Nakase met with Williams in 2025 in Turkey to pitch her on coming to Golden State. But the Seattle Storm cored Williams that offseason, guaranteeing Seattle exclusive negotiating rights with the French national. Williams remembers when she heard Lacob make his proclamation in 2023. "I was impressed, and I was enticed. It was like, this is a team I could want to play for one day," Williams said. "I thought I would finish my career in Seattle, but hearing that made me think a little bit. This guy is not playing around; he wants to win. That was eye-opening to me."

When Williams became a free agent, the Valkyries contacted her again, and Lacob joined Nakase and Nyanin in the recruitment.

"He said, 'This is why we are going to win. This is why it would be silly for you to go anywhere else. This is why we're going to have longevity. I want to build dynasties here,'" Williams said.

"Who doesn't want to come to something like that? We play this game to win championships. I've never won one, and at this point in my career, that is the top priority. ... I was so convinced that I would not win anywhere else."

One day after signing Williams, the Valkyries made another trajectory-shifting acquisition, landing Kiah Stokes after she spent four seasons and won three titles with Las Vegas, where she played alongside A'ja Wilson every day and under Nakase for one year. After Iliana Rupert announced that she would miss the 2026 season due to pregnancy, Stokes started every game, defending Angel Reese in the Finals.

Nyanin knew that these players could unlock a new level of her team. What has surprised the GM, though, is how quickly it has come together.

"You just never know if that's going to work out," Nyanin said.

It has. Williams, who was named Finals MVP thanks to a 30-point performance in Game 7, is having the best season of her career. She averaged a career-best 14.4 points and shot 34.2% from 3 -- and also finished second in Defensive Player of the Year voting and received WNBA All-Defensive first-team honors. She became the engine for Golden State's top-ranked defense, while also stepping up to be the shotmaker the Valkyries needed.

"The best part has been coming to work every day and enjoying it. Like, actually, that's a huge part of contending," Williams said. "When the playoffs started, our motivation was just -- we didn't want to stop playing together. We wanted to go as deep as we could because we knew this is the last time we could have a group like this. It's been really healing for me. It's made this season really special."

Down late in a win-or-go-home Game 3 in the first round against the Dallas Wings, Thornton pulled Burton, Williams and Kaila Charles into a huddle beneath their basket. They put their arms around each other and took a collective breath.

"It's just one of those things where [it was] an awareness of what we need," Burton said. "And in that moment, we needed to take an exhale and be together and just be present. ... That's pouring into each other and building each other up."

As Nyanin watched from the tunnel -- and as that sigh fueled their comeback and offered a glimpse of the composure Golden State, a team with no All-WNBA player selections, has possessed since its inception, Nyanin knew that all of the pieces she put together fit perfectly.

"That was the epitome of things we have said to them here and there," Nyanin said. "In that moment, all of the little things we have put together, I took a breath as well just to say yes, they will fight with each other and for each other. That's exactly why I am doing the job I am doing."

NAKASE WOULDN'T LET her players pick up a ball for the first three days of training camp this season.

There was no shooting, no running plays, no offense. The first three days of camp were dedicated to defense.

"That's when I knew this was going to be different," Burton said.

Those early sessions set the tone for what Nakase would demand: consistent defensive intensity, attention to detail and execution on the game plan. It also gave her players a taste of the kind of coach she is -- one who plays battle sounds during practice and calls her players "killers," doesn't allow for celebrations, and believes that cursing just means you're telling the truth.

Even when Nakase's behavior seems jarring -- or as she puts it, extreme -- she has built an environment that encourages her players to speak up and feel respected. It's why they so willingly buy into Nakase's vision and style.

"She's so authentic," Williams said. "We know her intentions are to put us in the best position to win. ... She's passionate. And sometimes we laugh at her, but we also check on her ... it's the love we have for each other."

When Williams arrived in Golden State, she told Nakase that sometimes her delivery was confusing. Others have told Nakase that they needed more time to celebrate the smaller wins. Her coaching staff urged her to take more care of herself so she can be a better leader.

All of this experience has led the Valkyries here, to their first title. Nakase's focus on defense made Golden State's unit the top ranked in the league through the regular season -- holding opponents to a league-low 75.1 points per game -- and second best in the playoffs. Stokes had 31 blocked shots this postseason, tied with Lisa Leslie for the most in WNBA history.

And her players' feedback has pushed Nakase to be a better version of herself -- and helped turn around the Finals when Golden State trailed 2-1. After the first three games of the series, she gave herself an F-minus score on her coaching because her communication was poor. So she turned to her players to see how she -- and in turn they -- could be better.

"You can give the best scheme in the world, but if your players don't want to follow it, it's not going to be successful," Stokes said. "Her willingness to listen to us and our ideas about what we think we're best at and what we can do, that's one thing that has jumped out to me; her willingness to adapt to her players."

Heading into Game 4, Nakase inserted Hayes and Kaila Charles into the starting lineup in place of Thornton and Zandalasini, respectively. Charles finished the game with a plus-14, and Hayes added 13 points -- and the change led to a massive momentum shift in the series, with the Valkyries taking the next two games.

"The best thing about our team is no one cares who starts, no one cares," Nakase said. "We can do that because we have a really selfless team, ego-less team."

"She's a great coach for a reason," Charles. "We trust our coach, so whatever she sees, we'll execute."

As Nakase walked out of her first interview with Lacob, she pledged to herself not to let his WNBA team fail. When she began to work alongside Nyanin, she promised her that they wouldn't let each other fail. As she opened up each season with her players, Nakase made sure they had every piece of support they needed.

All of this has led to history, and the Valkyries winning a title far sooner than anyone -- even Lacob -- could have ever predicted.

"Of course this is unbelievable," Lacob said Saturday night as the Valkyries celebrated. "Two years? It's insane."

stories.headline: Chris Fagan to join the Blues as director of coaching in 2027
stories.summary: Triple premeirship coach Chris Fagan has made the call on his AFL future, joining Carlton as their director of coaching for 2027.
stories.body:
Triple premeirship coach Chris Fagan has made the call on his AFL future, joining Carlton as their director of coaching for 2027.

The 65-year-old stepped down as Brisbane's senior coach after the club's 2026 premiership win -- it's third in a row -- with an aim to return closer to family.

Announced by the Blues on Saturday morning, Fagan will oversee a matchday role and begin mentoring the coaching panel to "establish development pathways for the coaches and help drive an elite, sustainable football program".

Fagan said he was looking forward to making a "real impact" at the Blues.

"While I loved my 10 years as a Senior Coach, this is a role I am passionate about and where I know I can have a real impact in this next phase of my football career," Fagan said in a statement.

"Supporting people to get the absolute best out of themselves is what I love most about football, so the chance to now be able to do that on a full-time basis is incredibly exciting. I can't wait to connect with each person in the football department, and in particular work closely with Josh to help every coach and player be the best Carlton person they can possibly be.

"In all my conversations with [the club] before accepting the role, what resonated strongly was how aligned they were on how to make Carlton a great football club. They shared a clear vision of evolving Carlton into a club that can contend but most importantly, they understand there is still significant work to do to get there.

"To have the senior leadership of a football club share such clarity in their direction, combined with a role that gives me genuine purpose, makes joining Carlton an opportunity too good to pass up."

Meanwhile Carlton's GM of Football Chris Davies said the appointment was an important one to support first-time senior coach Josh Fraser.

"We want to build our football club around good people and they do not come any better than Chris Fagan," Davies said.

"Few in the game have his wealth of experience and ability to connect with and get the best out of those around him. Most importantly, he is a proven winner who knows what it takes to build a consistently high-performing environment.

"Chris and Josh have built a connection in recent weeks over a shared philosophy of putting people first and building a program the right way. With Chris on board, Josh will be well supported, our coaches will be well developed and our program will continue to build the clarity and discipline required to be truly elite.

"We can't wait to welcome Chris and his wife Ursula, their daughters Jessica and Ellen and the entire Fagan family to Carlton."

...more to come.

stories.headline: Tonga learn semifinal fate after pipping Samoa
stories.summary: A late try to Addin Fonua-Blake has helped Tonga beat Samoa 20-18 and secure a World Cup semi-final against New Zealand.
stories.body:
Tonga have claimed victory in a World Cup battle for the ages, defeating bitter rivals Samoa in a 20-18 thriller to set up a semi-final showdown with New Zealand.

Kristian Woolf's side kept their undefeated group-stage record intact after Cronulla prop Addin Fonua-Blake crossed in the 72nd minute to snatch victory at CommBank Stadium in front of 29,411.

Tonga will face the Kiwis in Newcastle on Saturday in what will be the first World Cup meeting between the two nations since the 2017 tournament, which was characterised by the Jason Taumalolo-led defections to the Pacific nations.

Taumalolo was impressive for Tonga on Sunday night but Samoa gave their Polynesian brethren a major leg-up by missing three of their four conversion attempts.

"That's one of those things that happens in rugby league," said Samoa coach Ben Gardiner.

"But I'm very happy with the level of performance, the intensity and the way we went about our business."

Samoa outscored Tonga four tries to three, but Chanel Harris-Tavita and Ronald Volkman could only land one goal between them.

Harris-Tavita came off midway through the second half, clutching at a hamstring after missing a shot at goal and now appears unlikely to line up for Samoa against Australia in the other semi-final.

It looked as if things were going to be straightforward for Tonga, who had the upper hand for much of the first half but only had an 8-4 lead to show for it.

Wingers Dallin Watene-Zelezniak and Jojo Fifita both crossed but had tries chalked off on review before Sydney Roosters star Rob Toia continued his incredible run of form to score Tonga's opener in the 26th minute.

Haumole Olakau'atu ran over the top of Samoan five-eighth Jarome Luai before getting the ball away to Toia, who raced home from 50m out and dotted down under the sticks.

Halfback Isaiya Katoa converted then added a penalty after Jermaine McEwen was ruled to have interfered at the ruck.

But late in the first half, Luai put up a fifth-tackle kick that was batted back to Stephen Crichton, who flicked a late offload away for Brian To'o to score.

Fifita hit back for Tonga soon into the second half before Harris-Tavita flicked another Luai kick out to To'o to keep Samoa in the game.

Harris-Tavita struck the upright with his attempt then winced as he grabbed at his left hamstring.

Volkman was thrown into the action and the substitute No.6 was soon called upon to take a conversion which offered the chance to tie the game up.

It came after Luai and Sua Fa'alogo combined down the left before Hamiso Tabuai-Fidow finished the move.

Volkman was unable to add the extra points but pushed his side ahead when he pinballed through some tired Tonga defenders to score. He then converted his own try, with less than 12 minutes left.

But just as Samoa looked set to hang on, Fonua-Blake rampaged through the middle of the defence to snatch victory for Tonga.

"This group can do anything," Woolf said.

"We left four tries out there - two in the second half - and we've got plenty of improvement left in us.

"We keep heading on the right track but they (this team) can do anything."

Nov. 1: Wright to Nashville, Wood to Seattle
A pair of players once central to their former franchise's plans were moved Sunday in a deal involving the Nashville Predators and the Seattle Kraken.

The Predators traded winger Matthew Wood to the Kraken in exchange for center Shane Wright. The trade itself was a 1-for-1 swap involving two teams that are each vying for a playoff spot as American Thanksgiving gets closer.

Here's a quick glance at what it all means.

Nashville Predators

Grade: B+
You will hear the words "potential" and "potentially" a lot regarding this trade. That's what happens any time two teams choose to move on from a pair of forward that are still in their early 20s who were each, at one time, thought to be part of a blueprint going forward.

Wood and Wright both struggled to start the season. Wood has three points in 14 games while Wright has four in 14. But this trade potentially provides the Predators a player who is more of a known profile.

The reason Wright has been the subject of trade rumors the past few years goes back to the potential he showed as a draft prospect -- he was taken fourth overall in 2022 -- and during the 2024-25 season, when he had 19 goals and 44 points in 79 games. It was a strong baseline for a player who previously had 16 games of NHL experience over the previous two years because of a stop-start development process.

Even though he had only 12 goals and 27 points the next season, it at least proved he can reach double figures. Furthermore, he recorded double figures for a team that, over a two-year cycle, has been in the bottom 10 of goals per game.

It's likely that Nashville will slot Wright in as the second-line center, with Ryan O'Reilly, Jack Drury and Alexander Kerfoot as the other pivots. They are hoping to return to the playoffs for the first time since the 2024, when they were eliminated in the first round.

Seattle Kraken

Grade: B+
Wright became expendable for a few reasons, including inconsistencies since that promising 19-goal campaign. But also because the Kraken have more productive options down the middle. Berkly Catton is second on the team in points (11), while Frederik Gaudreau leads them in goals (seven). Matty Beniers is averaging 0.50 points per game while logging the most ice time (17:43 per game) among Kraken forwards. And Chandler Stephenson, a natural center, has gone to wing and leads the Kraken with 12 points in 14 games.

Adding Wood provides the Kraken a natural winger who can provide secondary production while also providing some size on the wing; the former University of Connecticut star is listed at 6-foot-4 and 202 pounds. He is also adept at using his size to get to the net front.

Wood scored 17 goals and 30 points in his first full NHL season in 2025-26, and there's potential for more -- and can fit within the Kraken's team construct. While Wood does shoot from the perimeter, he is effective enough at getting into the low slot and net front too.

Pairing him with playmaking forwards like Beniers, Catton, Gaudreau and Stephenson, along with puck-moving defensemen such as Vince Dunn and Brandon Montour, could lead to him hitting the 20-goal benchmark.

Oct. 23: Hellebuyck lands with Devils
Technically speaking, Connor Hellebuyck's suspension from the Winnipeg Jets did end Friday. It just had a different outcome with the three-time Vezina Trophy winner being traded to the New Jersey Devils.

Hellebuyck, who won the Hart Trophy in 2025, will go to the Devils in exchange for forward Dawson Mercer, forward Nick Bjugstad, goaltender Nico Daws, prospect center Alexander Command, a 2027 seventh-round pick and a 2029 second-round pick.

Let's take a look at what this means for both teams and how each front office performed:

New Jersey Devils

Grade: A
How Devils general manager Sunny Mehta arrived at this place goes back to one of his earliest moves. He knew the going rate to acquire a starting goaltender based on the return New Jersey received in late June when Mehta traded Jacob Markstrom to the Florida Panthers. Markstrom's trade brought back a return of three forwards. It was a move that gave Mehta, or any GM, more insight into what it would take to land arguably the greatest goaltender of his generation in Hellebuyck.

Trading Markstrom is also the reason acquiring Hellebuyck -- or any proven No. 1 goalie -- became a priority for New Jersey. That became even more evident with how the Devils started the regular season. Opening their first 10 games with a goaltending tandem of Jake Allen and Daws had the Devils entering Friday in the second and final Eastern Conference wild-card spot -- with the context that they appear to be a much better team than their place in the standings shows.

New Jersey has one of the strongest defensive structures in the NHL this season. The Devils came into the weekend allowing the second-fewest high-danger scoring chances per 60, the third-fewest scoring chances per 60, and the 10th-fewest shots per 60.

They also have a 59.74% shot share in 5-on-5 play. That figure is so strong that only the defending Stanley Cup champion Carolina Hurricanes (59.79% shot share) have held on to the puck more than the Devils in 5-on-5 play. So how is it that a team that controls the puck and limits high-danger chances, scoring chances and shots is in the last wild-card spot? Especially when it averages the 12th-most goals per game?

An argument could be had that it's because of the Devils' goaltending. They have the 13th-lowest team save percentage in 5-on-5 play at 89.95%. Across all scenarios, they have an .880 team save percentage, tied for the 23rd in the league.

Placing Hellebuyck, who has faced the second-most shots in the NHL since 2021-22, in New Jersey's system could see the Devils win more frequently by pairing his skills with their defensive infrastructure. And if it does? That's the possibility that Mehta and the Devils are banking on: that Hellebuyck can help them emerge as a legitimate threat to challenge in the Eastern Conference and perhaps have serious designs on winning a Stanley Cup this season.

That's the short-term view of how this can be digested. The long-term view is that the Devils, barring some sort of massive change, are going to be expected to challenge for a Stanley Cup with the 33-year-old Hellebuyck under contract for four more years at $8.5 million annually.

Building around homegrown talents such as Jesper Bratt, Nico Hischier and Jack Hughes has been a process. The Devils have used a variety of avenues from free agency to trades to build what they believe is the best possible team around a core that has since added another homegrown player in Luke Hughes. There have been times when the Devils look like they've been ready to aspire to more. But then there have been those moments when they've been left to ask probing questions about how they reach their desired destination.

Getting Hellebuyck has changed the conversation. Hellebuyck missing training camp because of his suspension means there is likely going to be an adjustment period. Nonetheless, adding the best version of Hellebuyck to a team that has proved it can consistently score and defend makes the Devils look like they're on the verge of something major. But the regular season, while important, isn't where this trade will ultimately be judged. The verdict will come in the playoffs, as the franchise seeks to win a Stanley Cup -- one of the few accolades Hellebuyck doesn't already have in his collection.

Winnipeg Jets

Grade: B+
Any deal Jets GM Kevin Cheveldayoff was going to reach for Hellebuyck was one that had to help the franchise both immediately and for the foreseeable future. It appears this particular trade has a chance to do both, with the caveat that it was always going to be a challenge to find the perfect return for the best player the Jets have drafted over the past 20 years.

That's why the place to start is with what it could mean for the Jets right now. Scoring was so much of an issue for the Jets in the 2025-26 season that three players -- Kyle Connor, Mark Scheifele and Gabriel Vilardi -- combined to score 40% of Winnipeg's goals. It was a drastic contrast compared with the 2024-25 season, when the Jets won the Presidents' Trophy largely due to contributions from different parts of their lineup.

Scoring, at least to start the season, remains an issue. The Jets came into Friday ranking 25th in the league in goals per game at a rate of 2.60 per contest. Adding to those scoring challenges is how they've struggled to consistently create opportunities when they've had the puck. They are averaging the 12th-fewest shots per 60, the 13th-fewest scoring chances per 60 and remain around league average in terms of high-danger chances per 60. Plus, the Jets have the 11th-lowest shot share in 5-on-5 play at 47.30%.

Expecting Mercer to be the lone solution to those problems isn't realistic. But it's fair to expect that he'll help by providing another option beyond Connor, Scheifele and Vilardi. Mercer is a three-time 20-goal scorer who finished last season with 20 goals and 42 points while averaging 18:13 in ice time. That level of production would have made him the Jets' fourth-leading goal scorer and had him fifth on the team in points.

Mercer, who has one year of team control remaining after this season, has zero goals and four assists through 10 games. The 24-year-old's ability to attain consistency is likely going to play an important role in a campaign that appears already to be at a sensitive stage. Winnipeg entered Friday with the same points total as the Colorado Avalanche for the second and final Western Conference wild-card spot.

The Avalanche have a Central Division-leading plus-10 goal differential. The four teams in the division that are either tied with or ahead of the Jets in the standings also have positive goal differentials, whereas the Jets currently sit at minus-3, having lost their past four games.

Bjugstad, who had six goals and nine points in 61 games last season, is still recovering from offseason pectoral muscle surgery that saw him begin the season on injured reserve. His initial diagnosis had him set to return at some point in the next four to six months, which places his earliest return around January. Bjugstad is in the final year of his contract, and it's possible he could once again be a deadline day departure should the Jets seek draft capital if they're out of the playoff chase. The Jets have 28 draft picks over the next three years after the Hellebuyck trade.

Daws, who is 2-2 with a 2.78 goals-against average and a .874 save percentage, is joining a team that has the fourth-highest save percentage in 5-on-5 play. He provides the Jets with a more proven alternative in net should they need it. The Jets have used Clay Stevenson in tandem with Stuart Skinner, but Stevenson came into this season with five games of NHL experience, whereas Daws already had 55 games and is more than familiar with the demands of being in a tandem at this level.

Getting Command, the 12th pick in the 2026 draft, gives the Jets another potential top-six or top-nine option for the future as he continues to develop in Sweden. Command has seven goals and 12 points playing in the under-20 Nationell against younger competition, while he has no points in six games while playing for Orebro in the Swedish Hockey League, the strongest league in the Swedish hockey system.

Sept. 28: Marchenko to the Leafs, Knies to the Blue Jackets
Less than 24 hours before the start of a new season, the NHL had its first blockbuster trade with the Blue Jackets trading Kirill Marchenko to the Maple Leafs.

Marchenko, along with forward Miles Wood and goaltender Elvis Merzlikins, heads to Toronto in exchange for forwards Matthew Knies and Steven Lorentz, defenseman Emil Andrae and a conditional 2027 second-round pick. Columbus will retain 18% of Merzlikins' salary.

Here's a look at how both teams fared:

Toronto Maple Leafs

Grade: A-
Maybe the easiest -- and most important -- place to start is with Marchenko signing a six-year contract carrying a $12.5 million average annual value. Attaining cost certainty is always going to be key for teams, especially in this current landscape in which the price for a player's services is subject to change with each new contract. This holds true for Marchenko.

He was under contract for one more year at $3.85 million, and one more year of team control as a pending restricted free agent. That left any team acquiring him facing one of two hypotheticals:

Would it be better for them to trade for Marchenko, let him play out the season, see how he looks in their lineup and then sign him to a long-term deal?
Or do they get a sign-and-trade done so they have him locked in for several years at what they believe is a manageable cost -- at a time when every class of player is going to cash in, with top-line players at the top of that list?

Choosing the second option allowed the Leafs to avoid the seasonlong dilemma of deliberating on a long-term deal. That could prove to be a vital decision, with the expectation that Marchenko's stats are likely to surge while playing alongside Auston Matthews for at least two seasons. Because although Marchenko played with talented centers in his time with the Blue Jackets, some believe he could reach the 40-goal mark for the first time in his career playing with the Leafs superstar. His career high is 31, scored in 2024-25.

His addition sets the Leafs up to have a first line with Jack Roslovic joining Matthews and Marchenko, while having a second line featuring William Nylander, John Tavares and rookie Gavin McKenna, the Penn State forward who was the first pick in the 2026 draft.

Matthews' future is another subject for another time. Yet when it comes to Marchenko? Getting him signed long term provides the Leafs with more certainty. He is the seventh player on their active roster who has more than three years of team control remaining.

Other elements of this trade will come under question. That starts with whether it was prudent to add more to their salary cap starting next season knowing Knies, who is entering the second year of a six-year contract, was already on the roster at a cheaper salary of $7.75 million annually.

Then there are Merzlikins and Wood. Merzlikins is currently on IR after undergoing offseason shoulder surgery. He's in the final year of his contract worth $4.428 million. When healthy, he's another option for the Leafs in goal. But they could also move on from him later in the season to get help elsewhere. Wood, who went unclaimed on waivers, gives the Leafs a potential depth forward if needed.

Columbus Blue Jackets

Grade: B+
There's a challenge facing every front office that has a star player who wants out of town. Of course there will be other teams who want the player in question. Whether any of the proposed deals make sense usually ends up being the biggest hurdle to clear.

That's what makes this particular trade for the Blue Jackets one that could work. Why? Because of how they stand to benefit both now and in the future.

Moving on from Marchenko, who led the Blue Jackets with 27 goals and was second with 67 points last season, meant Columbus had to find a comparable winger in return. Knies appears to be just that. The 23-year-old, who had 23 goals and 66 points last season, gives the Blue Jackets a sizable option on the edge who can generate offensive opportunities in a top-six role. Knies will face questions about how his production will fare without Matthews, but his ability to attack the net could prove critical for a Columbus team that was in the top 10 in scoring chances per 60 minutes but was around league average in high-danger chances per 60.

Columbus could use Knies on its top line next to Adam Fantilli and Kent Johnson, while having a second line featuring Conor Garland, Sean Monahan and Valeri Nichushkin, who arrived this summer in trade.

Knies' $7.75 million AAV also helps, as Fantilli is set to earn $13.75 million annually starting this season. In total, Columbus has seven players set to make more than $7 million annually who have four or more years left on their current deals.

Beyond Knies, Lorentz provides the Blue Jackets with another proven option they can use in various spots as needed. He scored seven goals and 18 points in 71 games last season after eight and 19 in 2024-25, his first campaign with the Leafs. And while the Blue Jackets do have a bottom six in place, Lorentz gives them someone who logged more than 158 short-handed minutes last season; this could prove beneficial for a team that was 28th on the penalty kill last season.

Emil Andrae -- who was already traded once this offseason, from Philly back on June 16 -- is an option on the back end. He had 13 points in 61 games with the Flyers last season.
